title: Simes error control for two-sided Gaussian tests
decision_reason: Explicit exact conjecture, independent specialist discussion, scoped current counterexamples, duplicate screening and separated A41 self-review passed.

problem_fingerprint.objects: Every positive integer n, real symmetric positive semidefinite n by n correlation matrix Sigma with diagonal entries 1, and X distributed N_n(0,Sigma).
problem_fingerprint.model: All coordinates have zero means and known unit marginal variances. The correlation matrix is arbitrary and fixed; no sample covariance is estimated.
problem_fingerprint.observable: P_i=2 Phi(-|X_i|), increasingly ordered as P_(1),...,P_(n); S_n=min_{1<=k<=n} n P_(k)/k.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For every such n and Sigma and every fixed alpha in (0,1).
problem_fingerprint.normalization_checks: Each marginal P_i is uniform. The statistic already belongs to [0,1] because its k=n term is P_(n). Rank thresholds are k alpha/n. A positive-definite formulation extends to semidefinite matrices by Gaussian weak convergence, since rejection boundaries lie in finitely many sets P_i=k alpha/n of marginal probability zero.
problem_fingerprint.scope_limits: Two-sided unweighted Gaussian global-null test. Not one-sided Gaussian copulas, nonzero mean configurations, Student t statistics, asymptotic alpha-only control, covariance-adjusted procedures, or arbitrary non-Gaussian uniform p-values.

independent_corroboration.assessment: Sarkar explicitly identifies the conjecture for the unweighted Simes global test; authors are disjoint from CRW25. This is independent scholarly corroboration, not an independent review of this draft.
independent_corroboration.currency: 2023/2025 source status checked against July–August 2026 results and unrestricted/current-year searches.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Gaussian copulas obtained by coordinatewise monotone transforms.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Taking absolute values folds the distribution; Remark 11 expressly separates this conjecture. Its asymptotic small-alpha and inflated bounds are not the exact all-alpha target.

resolution_scope_comparisons.source: S98 Theorem 3.1; S08 Theorem 3.1 and discussion
resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: MTP2 dependence; for absolute Gaussian vectors a sufficient condition is nonpositive off-diagonal entries of D Sigma^{-1} D for some diagonal sign matrix D.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: The covariance restriction is not automatic. For example, the valid 3-by-3 correlation matrix with off-diagonals (0.4,0.4,-0.1) has inverse off-diagonal signs (-,-,+); their product cannot become negative under sign changes. The title 'proof of the Simes conjecture' therefore does not resolve the arbitrary-correlation formulation.
resolution_scope_comparisons.inference: The explicit three-dimensional diagnostic and sign-product argument are catalogue scope checks, not new literature results.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Squared statistics are rescaled using 1-R_i^2 and the first critical value solves a covariance-dependent equation.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Different statistics and critical values. Specializing every mean to zero retains those changes and does not recover the original rule.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: 100N coordinates: 96N zero means, N means 12/5, and 3N means 22/5, with a specified positive-definite factor covariance; general-configuration FDR exceeds nominal level.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Four percent non-null coordinates. The required all-zero mean hypothesis fails; no global-null counterexample is asserted.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Worst-case FDR over means and correlation matrices; construction includes positive masses of primary and secondary non-null coordinates.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Not an all-null result. The same paper proves MTP2 for the centered null block in its one-factor class, consistent with Simes validity there. No conversion to the requested counterexample follows.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Conditional-variance-dependent upper bounds for the ordinary rule and guarantees for modified shifted/calibrated procedures, including independent covariance estimation.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: The ordinary-rule upper bound need not be alpha. The calibrated procedures change the question; zero means alone do not yield the desired inequality from these bounds.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: All-null triangular arrays of uniform p-values generated by a discrete choice of subset followed by draws from restricted intervals.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Not the stipulated joint Gaussian construction. Its pairs have zero simultaneous probability below alpha/n. A pair of unit-variance centered Gaussians has positive probability of simultaneous sufficiently large absolute values, including the perfectly correlated cases; thus these p-value pairs cannot be folded Gaussian. This incompatibility is a direct scope inference.
The linking inequality still depends on null-block Simes error; consistency only requires vanishing error as alpha tends to zero. Neither supplies the exact finite-alpha Gaussian inequality.

nearest.difference: Independence of polynomial statistics from moment identities, not a rank-based rejection probability.
Optimal Gaussian partitions under correlated noise, not error control for a prescribed test.
